research_rationale: EO 9674 (January 4, 1946) created a Director of Liquidation and a Liquidation Advisory Committee in the Office for Emergency Management to further the winding up of the war agencies. It has no own-terms sunset. EO 9744 of June 27, 1946 provides that the office of the Director of Liquidation and the Liquidation Advisory Committee, established by Executive Order No. 9674, together with their functions, "are hereby terminated", and states that it becomes effective on June 30, 1946. The status is NO: the bodies and every function the order gave them were terminated effective June 30, 1946, and no held source revives them.
savings_reason: EO 9744 directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, consonant with applicable law, to make suitable disposition of the records and property in the possession of the Director of Liquidation. That residual disposition duty is a new command of EO 9744, not a continuation of EO 9674, and no held source preserves any other EO 9674 clause.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: EO 9674 states no date, condition or sunset for the Director or the Committee. The held number search found only EO 9744 (and a duplicate Federal Register page that reprints it) acting on EO 9674; the OFR catalog note naming EO 9744 (June 27, 1946) as the revoking order agrees with the held text. No earlier abolition of this Office is shown by a held source. Paragraph 3 of the order says the Director's functions do not reach agencies already abolished, which limits his reach but ends no clause.
scope_check: EO 9744 terminates the office of the Director of Liquidation and the Liquidation Advisory Committee together with the functions of the Director and the Committee, which are exactly what paragraphs 1, 2(a)-(f), 3 and 4 of EO 9674 create or limit, so every clause ends. The termination is stated as effective June 30, 1946 (signing June 27, 1946).
independent_command_check: Each clause is a continuing duty or authority of the Director or the Committee, or a limiting rule on them, with no performance date in the order. No held source shows any of them performed or exhausted before June 30, 1946, so the stated effective termination is the first established end of each.
savings_check: EO 9744 directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, consonant with applicable law, to make suitable disposition of the records and property in the possession of the Director of Liquidation. That residual disposition duty is a new command of EO 9744, not a continuation of EO 9674, and no held source preserves any other EO 9674 clause.

research_rationale: EO 9680 (January 17, 1946) abolished the United States of America Typhus Commission, established by EO 9285 of December 24, 1942, and directed the Secretary of War to supervise its liquidation. The order states the abolition is as of June 30, 1946, a date fixed by its own terms, and has a single paragraph of operative text (abolition) plus a liquidation direction. The status is NO: by its own terms the commission was abolished as of June 30, 1946, a self-executing abolition, and no held source revives it. The ending source is the order's own operative text; the creating order EO 9285 is the held record that identifies the body abolished.
savings_reason: The order itself provides that the liquidation of the commission's affairs and the disposition of its records and scientific data are to be accomplished under the supervision of the Secretary of War; that residual liquidation function is carried by the Secretary of War and is the only savings-type provision in the order. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 9680.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end: the order itself fixes June 30, 1946 and the held records show no earlier instrument touching the Typhus Commission after EO 9285 (the OFR catalog gives only the cross-reference to EO 9285). The held text of EO 9285 is only the creating order, not an ending, so the end rests on the abolition paragraph of EO 9680. The dispatch note that EO 9285 text is a recheck copy does not affect the end, which is read from EO 9680 itself.
scope_check: The single operative paragraph abolishes the whole commission and directs liquidation under the Secretary of War; the inventory has one clause (the whole operative text), which includes both the abolition and the liquidation direction, and both end by the stated date.
independent_command_check: The abolition is a one-time self-executing act with a stated effective date. The liquidation direction is a task that follows the abolition and is tied to it; no held source shows when liquidation finished, so it is not given a separate later end, and the order is dated by the stated abolition date.
savings_check: The order itself provides that the liquidation of the commission's affairs and the disposition of its records and scientific data are to be accomplished under the supervision of the Secretary of War; that residual liquidation function is carried by the Secretary of War and is the only savings-type provision in the order. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 9680.

research_rationale: EO 11726 (June 29, 1973) established the Energy Policy Office in the Executive Office of the President under a Director, set the Director's responsibilities, provided expenses and support, set a report date of March 15, 1974, and superseded EO 11712 (abolishing the Special Committee on Energy and the National Energy Office). EO 11748 of December 4, 1973 (Federal Energy Office) superseded EO 11726 only "to the extent that it is inconsistent" with it. EO 11775 of March 26, 1974 states that the Energy Policy Office was continued in being on an interim basis to permit an orderly transition, and abolishes it and supersedes EO 11726 in its Section 1. The status is NO: the Office was abolished and the order superseded on March 26, 1974, and no held source revives it.
savings_reason: EO 11775 Sec. 2 amends Section 8 of Proclamation No. 3279 so that the Administrator of the Federal Energy Office chairs the Oil Policy Committee, continues the Committee as reconstituted, and transfers personnel, property, records and funds for the functions moved from the Director of the Energy Policy Office; Sec. 3 directs the Administrator of General Services to wind up the Office and return unobligated funds to the Emergency Fund of the President. Those functions and funds accrue to the Federal Energy Office and the Fund; no other EO 11726 command is preserved.
earlier_end_check: The partial supersession by EO 11748 Sec. 6 (December 4, 1973) reaches only provisions inconsistent with EO 11748, and no held source identifies which clause of EO 11726 it extinguished: EO 11775 itself recites that the Energy Policy Office was continued on an interim basis after EO 11748 until the transition was completed. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an endpoint needs a reason shown by evidence, so EO 11748 is recorded as a later event (partial supersession), not a first end, and the first established end of every clause is EO 11775, March 26, 1974. No own-terms end exists: the March 15, 1974 report date in Sec. 4 is a deadline, not an end. A formal reviewer should note the possibility that some clauses were displaced between December 4, 1973 and March 26, 1974; the held evidence does not show it.
scope_check: EO 11775 Sec. 1 abolishes the Energy Policy Office as a whole and supersedes Executive Order No. 11726 of June 29, 1973 with no in-part qualifier. The corrected inventory has 19 clauses: Sec. 1, Sec. 2(a), the lead of Sec. 2(b) and items (1) to (10), Sec. 3(a) to (c), Sec. 4 and Sec. 5. Sec. 5, which superseded EO 11712 and abolished two other bodies, was a self-executing act performed on signing.
independent_command_check: Sec. 5 (supersedure of EO 11712 and abolition of the Special Committee on Energy and the National Energy Office) is a one-time self-executing command performed on June 29, 1973, so its first end is the signing date, not the later abolition of the Energy Policy Office. Sec. 4 is a report deadline (March 15, 1974); the held sources do not show the report was made, and a deadline is not an end, so Sec. 4 is carried with the other continuing commands to the abolition.
savings_check: EO 11775 Sec. 2 amends Section 8 of Proclamation No. 3279 so that the Administrator of the Federal Energy Office chairs the Oil Policy Committee, continues the Committee as reconstituted, and transfers personnel, property, records and funds for the functions moved from the Director of the Energy Policy Office; Sec. 3 directs the Administrator of General Services to wind up the Office and return unobligated funds to the Emergency Fund of the President. Those functions and funds accrue to the Federal Energy Office and the Fund; no other EO 11726 command is preserved.

research_rationale: EO 11728 (July 12, 1973) amended section 104(b)(1) of EO 11157 (incentive pay for hazardous duty involving aerial flight) to require 2 hours of aerial flight in a calendar month, with carry-over of hours flown in the preceding five months. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 an amendment continues, amended, until the parent order ends. EO 11157 of June 22, 1964, as amended, was revoked by EO 13294 of March 28, 2003 (Sec. 2), which also delegates the underlying statutory authority (37 U.S.C. 301, 301a and 301c) to the Secretaries. The status is NO: the parent order carrying the amended section 104(b)(1) was revoked on March 28, 2003.
savings_reason: The held text of EO 13294 revokes EO 11157, as amended, without a savings clause preserving section 104(b)(1); its Sec. 3 is only a no-private-rights provision, and its Sec. 1 delegates the statutory authority to the Secretaries instead. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 11728.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: EO 11728 states no date, condition or sunset.
